findings.reason: the plan must name the one measure its closing census uses and give the earlier reading in that same measure, otherwise the section's own baseline line invites an improvement claim that neither reading establishes.
findings.text: the changed clause lays the closing census beside "8 forms over 32 flux-surface-average names" from §1 and "3 forms over 73 flux-surface-average names" from the live closing census as two comparable baselines, but the 8 is a count of distinct notation-style combinations in published-operator-census.txt (langle_plain+oint+gradpsi_weight 17, langle_sub+oint+gradpsi_weight 3, langle_sub+oint+Bp_weight 3, langle_plain+gradpsi_weight 3, langle_sub+oint 2, langle_sub+gradpsi_weight 2, langle_sub 1, langle_plain 1 — exactly 8), while the 3 is a count of distinct matched sentence texts under shared_part_form_counts, and the largest of those three forms is the `<omitted>` bucket holding 69 of the 73 names (rewrite-closing-census.json phases.live.operators.flux_surface_averaged: form_count 3, omitted_count 69, the other forms holding 1 name and 3 names), so the two figures count different quantities and the live one counts silence as a form while the published one counts only names that state the average — a §6 node comparing its closing count to both would report a 5-form improvement the instruments do not support and cannot tell whether the closure is measured on the sentence wording or on the notation style
